note: Passage 3706 (Pro 1:10) — 'if sinners entice you, do not consent.' The will's refusal (avah, negated) is the pivotal IB act; sinners = the enticing agents. Descent (the enticement) named honestly.

dims.v: sinners — those whose settled bent is to sin, here as enticers
the sinful who entice the son to join them
the son they seek to draw in
set against the son's refusal to consent
chatta = persons defined by sin; the danger the book warns of is not abstract evil but sinful companions who ENTICE. The threat is relational/social.
to consent — the will's yielding; here commanded NOT to yield
the act of the will refusing to yield to enticement (avah negated)
the counter-move to the sinners' enticement — will against pull

avah is the WILL itself — the decisive inner faculty. The book's first ethical command targets not knowledge but volition: 'do not consent.' Prohibition present (the negated will) though not a separate 113 here.
